{
  "claim": "In recover_json_object, fenced JSON objects with repeated keys are not resolved last-wins and are skipped; they can therefore lose to an earlier strict fenced object, violating the documented last-fenced-wins rule.",
  "expected": "recover_json_object should return the later fenced object with the repeated key resolved last-wins, e.g. ({'a': 2}, ('a',)).",
  "observed": "The fenced pool is searched in reverse; the later fenced object fails loads_strict because of duplicate keys, then parsed is forced to None because pool is fenced, so it is skipped. The earlier strict fenced object is returned as ({'a': 1}, ()).",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\": 1}\n```\n```json\n{\"a\": 1, \"a\": 2}\n```",
  "source_basis": "The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text ... A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable.",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Inputs to recover_json_object with at least one earlier strict-parseable fenced JSON object and a later fenced JSON object containing repeated keys.",
  "uncertainty": "The phrase 'when any fence holds one' could be read as strict-only, but the repeated-keys candidate rule removes that reading."
}
